title: This Seabird Flies 44,000 Miles a Year, Pole to Pole
subject: arctic tern

scenes.text: One small seabird flies from pole to pole, then turns around and does it again.
Scientists strapped 1.4-gram trackers to the legs of 60 arctic terns and followed them.
They breed in Greenland, then fly all the way to the Weddell Sea, next to Antarctica.
The route isn't a straight line. They loop in a giant S down the Atlantic.
The average trip was 44,000 miles a year. The longest was 50,700.
Over a lifetime, that adds up to about three trips to the Moon and back. Pole to pole, twice a year.

description:
One small seabird flies from pole to pole, then turns around and does it again.
Trackers weighing 1.4 grams showed an average round trip of 44,000 miles a year.
Would you have guessed a bird could out-travel a plane?
first_comment: Would you rather follow the summer like the tern, or stay put? And what animal should we track next?
